content:
On 2026-09-04 EVERY sub-task creation failed - memory_task_add(parent_id=...) and every memory_task_plan carrying a parent_index - with a DuckDB INTERNAL assertion: "Attempted to access index 0 within vector of size 0". The mandatory rule "Decompose a task into sub-tasks" was therefore unimplementable, and had been since sub-tasks shipped.

THE CULPRIT was one query in TaskRepository.next_position:
    SELECT COALESCE(MAX(position), -1) FROM tasks WHERE parent_id = ?
It crashes only when the parent has NO children yet - which is every parent's FIRST sub-task, i.e. the common case. The parent_id IS NULL branch alongside it is unaffected, because IS NULL takes a different path.

WHAT IT IS NOT, all four ruled out by experiment:
- Not the data and not the SQL: CREATE TABLE t2 AS SELECT * FROM tasks, then the IDENTICAL query on t2, returns -1 correctly. Same 31 rows, same schema.
- Not corruption a checkpoint clears: CHECKPOINT does not help.
- Not a stale secondary index: dropping idx_tasks_parent does not help.
- Not table size: 31 rows.
It is the PERSISTED tasks table's own storage metadata. A synthetic table built to the same DDL and populated the same way never reproduces it, at 10, 200 or 3000 rows, with or without CHECKPOINT or reopen. A filter value sorting OUTSIDE the column's statistics range (e.g. 'no-such-id') returns fine, while a real uuid sorting among the existing parent_ids crashes - consistent with the empty result arriving from a scanned row group rather than a pruned one. DuckDB 1.5.1; pyproject pins only duckdb>=1.1.0.

THE FIX is to not run an ungrouped aggregate over a filtered scan at all: select the positions and fold them in Python, max(..., default=-1) + 1. A plain SELECT position ... WHERE parent_id = ? is unaffected, and at these row counts the aggregate bought nothing.

WHY 627 PASSING TESTS MISSED IT, the part worth remembering: the suite HAS sub-task coverage and it passes, because fixtures build a fresh database per test and a freshly built table never carries whatever metadata triggers this. A test cannot reproduce it. So the protection is a source guard asserting next_position issues no MAX( in its SQL literals - reading the SQL string literals via AST, not the source text, because the docstring quotes the banned SQL and the fix itself calls Python's max().

GENERAL LESSON: a green suite on fixture-built databases says nothing about a query's behaviour against a long-lived file. When a bug survives a copy of the live database but not a rebuild of the same rows, stop looking at the data and suspect stored table state.
summary: On 2026-09-04 EVERY sub-task creation failed - memory_task_add(parent_id=
title: Sub-task creation crashed on a DuckDB aggregate; next_position must fold rows in Python

content: Each project has a project_uid (UUID) in the SQLite registry, written into .claude-memory/manifest.json as `project_id`. Because that file is committed, moving or renaming a project folder re-binds the existing project instead of registering a duplicate, and a teammate's clone resolves to the same project. Resolution order in ProjectService.claim_folder: uid match (matched/rebound) -> same-slug project bound to this same folder or with no uid (adopted) -> otherwise a new project on a free slug (created). detect_project_from_cwd checks the manifest uid first, then falls back to portable DB / bound path / folder name. The sync CLI calls POST /api/hook/claim before import or export, and session-start.sh runs `sync import` BEFORE auto-register so auto-register can never create the duplicate first.
summary: Each project has a project_uid (UUID) in the SQLite registry, written into
title: Project identity is the project_uid in the committed manifest, not the path

content:
Hit for real on 2026-09-04 while building the Asoode and Snap Muse boards; cost a full rebuild of 16 boards and 166 tasks.

`AsoodeClient.create_work_package(project_id, title, *, description, external_ref, board_template)` has NO `sub_project_id` parameter, even though asoode's `CreateWorkPackageDto` accepts `subProjectId`. A board created through the client therefore always lands at PROJECT ROOT with `subProjectId: null`, which looks fine in the API response and is only visible when you fetch the project and read `workPackages[].subProjectId`.

THERE IS NO WAY TO FIX IT AFTERWARDS. `EditWorkPackageDto` carries title/description/color/darkColor/beginAt/endAt only. `POST /work-packages/:id/connect/:projectId` moves a board between PROJECTS and does not touch `subProjectId`. So the only remedy is delete + recreate, which means recreating every task on it.

Workaround until the client gains the parameter:
    client._post(f"/work-packages/create/{project_id}", {
        "title": ..., "description": ..., "boardTemplate": BOARD_KANBAN,
        "subProjectId": sub_id, "externalRef": ref})

Two related traps found in the same session:
- `fetch_work_package(id)` returns `tasks: []` ALWAYS — it hydrates `lists` but not their tasks. Do not use it to verify that a task write landed; it will read as an empty board. Count with `POST /tasks/changes` instead, whose response key is `changes` (not `items`/`tasks`), or with `kartabl`.
- Sub-projects have no `externalRef`, so `POST /projects/:id/sub/create` is NOT idempotent. Match on title against `fetch_project(...)["subProjects"]` before creating, or a re-run silently makes a second one.

See [[asoode-bridge-idempotency]].
summary: Hit for real on 2026-09-04 while building the Asoode and Snap Muse boards; cost a full rebuild of 16 boards...
title: AsoodeClient.create_work_package cannot place a board in a sub-project — and nothing can move it later

content:
frontend/src/components/UpdateBanner.tsx is machine-wide state rendered above every view (App.tsx, top of the scroll container), built on the Integrations section idiom rather than a new banner style.

WHAT THE COPY MUST KEEP SAYING: pressing Update records approval; the Stop hook installs at the END of the turn, because installing reloads the launchd daemon and drops every live MCP connection. So the button says so BEFORE the click, and the banner flips to "Update approved / queued" immediately AFTER it. A button that looks inert for a minute gets pressed again - that is the entire reason this component exists rather than a toast.

FOUR STATES, and the two easy ones to get wrong are the last two:
1. update available -> the banner.
2. approved -> "nothing installed yet", Cancel update.
3. no update, no error -> render NOTHING.
4. no update WITH update:last_error -> the last CHECK failed. Amber "this is not a confirmation that you are up to date". Never render a failed check as being current - update_poller.py's docstring makes the same point for the same reason.
And when an update IS showing while last_error is set, say the newest check failed so this may be stale; "Checked 4m ago" otherwise implies freshness the data does not have.

THE STALE CLICK. update:status can flip between render and click, and POST /api/update/approve then 400s ("no update is available to approve"). Refetching after the failure REMOVES the banner, so an unexplained disappearance right after a click reads as success. It renders "Nothing was approved - that update is no longer on offer" with a Dismiss instead. Do not "simplify" that branch away.

Refresh is a 60s interval PLUS a window focus listener: the hook installs while the user is in the terminal and clears update:approved, so the banner must re-read on return.

API SHAPE TRAPS: last_checked_at is unix-epoch SECONDS as a string, not ISO, so lib/utils formatRelative cannot take it directly (checkedAgo converts). release_notes is null for the live github_commits source - only github_releases fills it. release_url is remote-sourced and is scheme-checked to http(s) before it reaches an href.
summary: The update banner promises approval, not installation, and has four states: frontend/src/components/UpdateBanner
title: The update banner promises approval, not installation, and has four states

content:
Decided 2026-09-03. memory-mcp is gaining a task concept. Key constraints agreed with the user:

1. memory-mcp MUST work fully without asoode. Some users won't run a PM app. So the local `tasks` tables in per-project DuckDB are a complete working task store (create, describe, assign, state, comments, time tracking) — NOT a thin ledger.
2. asoode integration is per-project, OPT-IN, and fully configurable. asoode is on-premise, so base_url / socket_url / project id / work package id are all per-link config. Never hardcode a host. Copy the gateway rule from project_service.py:66-67 — a project is never auto-bound, so private projects can't leak.
3. The asoode PAT is stored in app_settings['cred:<base_url>'] (registry.py:238-252), keyed by URL not project, and never enters the committable .claude-memory/ snapshot.
4. Offline-first: every mirrorable mutation appends to a `task_outbox` row and returns immediately. Connection loss is a normal state. On reconnect: drain outbox in order per task, then reconcile inbound.
5. Inbound uses a LIVE Socket.IO subscription (user's choice over polling), from a new asyncio task in daemon.build_app()'s lifespan. No such background mechanism exists today. This makes asoode's socket authentication a hard blocker. A reconcile poll runs on every reconnect since socket delivery is not durable.
6. Tasks live in DuckDB and NEVER enter the JSON snapshot. This is what kills the user's "JSON files could become 100MB+" worry. WARNING: SYNC_CATEGORIES is derived automatically (constants.py:24), so tasks must be separate TABLES, not a memory category — otherwise they start being written to .claude-memory/.
7. One claude project -> many asoode work packages is solved by a `project_links` table in the SQLite registry with a `match_paths` JSON column: in a monorepo, apps/backend/** routes to the backend board, apps/frontend/** to the frontend board.

Rejected: building a full task manager UI in memory-mcp to replace asoode (duplicates a product the user already owns, and memory-mcp is a single-Mac launchd daemon with no phone access and no team model). Also rejected: a pure bridge with no local storage (asoode has no externalRef field, so without local state every retry duplicates).

DuckDB-vs-JSON exchange question answered: neither — don't move files. DuckDB stays the local store, the wire is small incremental JSON over HTTP. Measured: a DuckDB file with ONE row is 5.26 MB (block allocation + persisted HNSW dominate, files never shrink); JSON snapshots are 22-650x smaller.

Full docs in docs/bridge/ (01 asoode analysis, 02 memory-mcp analysis, 03 Claude UI surfaces, 04 design decisions).
summary: Tasks module + optional asoode bridge: local-first, offline-tolerant: Decided 2026-09-03
title: Tasks module + optional asoode bridge: local-first, offline-tolerant

content:
app.asoode.com / api.asoode.com / socket.asoode.com are defaults in constants.py, not hardcoding: every read goes through asoode.get_endpoints() with precedence env > stored setting > default, and `sources` reports which one won. Setting only api_url derives the app./socket. siblings when the host looks like api.<domain>, and returns nothing rather than a guess otherwise. This revises design decision D2, which was written against an MCP whose default was localhost:3000 - a default that was wrong everywhere, unlike this one.

The PAT is keyed by API base URL in the SQLite registry's app_settings (reusing get_credential/set_credential), so it is machine-wide by construction: one entry covers every project, and switching to an on-premise URL and back does not lose the cloud token. It never enters the committable .claude-memory snapshot. It is write-only from outside the process - status(), the HTTP routes and the MCP tool return only a prefix+last4 fingerprint. There is deliberately NO MCP tool to set it, because a PAT pasted into a chat message stays in the transcript; the CLI reads it from a no-echo prompt or stdin, never argv. Also chmod 600 on registry.db, which was 644 while holding a credential.
summary: asoode: hosted endpoints by default, PAT stored once per machine: app
title: asoode: hosted endpoints by default, PAT stored once per machine

content:
db/connection.py has `transaction(slug)` for an operation that must be all-or-nothing. It publishes its connection on a CONTEXTVAR; `connect(slug)` inside that context yields that connection and does NOT close it. So all 40+ `with connect(project)` sites in the repositories join one transaction with ZERO signature changes. First caller: memory_task_plan (services/task_planner.py).

USE IT for any new multi-write operation. Do NOT thread a `conn=` parameter through repositories instead - that was considered and rejected: it only fixes the paths you remember to thread, must be redone for every future atomic operation, and changes a public repository contract for one caller.

FOUR CONSTRAINTS, each of which is a bug if broken:

1. `get_connection` must NEVER join. It hands ownership to a caller who closes it (portable_service.py, project_service.py); closing the transaction's connection mid-flight would be a new bug. Only `connect` joins.

2. It must stay RE-ENTRANT. DuckDB raises TransactionException "cannot start a transaction within a transaction" on a nested BEGIN, so a second transaction(slug) inside the first joins instead.

3. A CONTEXTVAR, not a thread-local and not a module global. Container._mirror_soon spawns a daemon thread (asoode-flush-<project>) on every task mutation, and a DuckDB connection is not safe to share across threads. A new thread starts from an EMPTY context, so it provably cannot pick ours up. Verified, not assumed. Precedent: context._request_user.

4. A ROLLBACK undoes local rows and NOTHING ELSE. It cannot un-POST to asoode. So anything remote or threaded goes through `after_commit(fn, key=...)`, which returns False when there is no transaction (meaning "run it yourself now"). TaskService._enqueue does exactly this: the outbox INSERT stays inside the transaction and rolls back with everything else, while the mirror nudge waits for the commit. Without that split, a plan failing on task 4 leaves three asoode cards with no local rows - the shape behind the 54-duplicate incident and the "A CLI write asks the daemon" rule.

Also do not wrap only part of a multi-step write: TaskRepository.next_position reads existing positions to append, and on a SEPARATE connection it is blind to uncommitted siblings and hands every task in a plan the same position.

MEASURED on duckdb 1.5.1 (pyproject says duckdb>=1.1.0, a floor - 1.1.x is untested): the same connection sees its own uncommitted rows; ROLLBACK is clean across close+reopen; a second in-process connection neither sees uncommitted rows nor blocks, and can write; a failed statement does NOT poison the transaction (so OutboxRepository.enqueue's swallow-and-return-"" is safe inside one); a nested BEGIN raises.

Tests: tests/test_transaction.py (the primitive), tests/services/test_task_planner.py::TestAPlanIsAllOrNothing and ::TestTheMirrorWaitsForTheCommit (the caller).

NOT everything multi-write wants this. task_bridge.py's asoode import loop is deliberately per-item: it returns created/updated/skipped counts so a partial import is legible, and each item does remote bookkeeping a local rollback could not undo. Making it atomic would discard 39 good imports because item 40 failed.
entities: A CLI write asks the daemon
summary: transaction(slug): making connection-per-operation repositories atomic: db/connection
title: transaction(slug): making connection-per-operation repositories atomic

content:
asoode broadcasts every change to every member of a work package and applies NO actor exclusion at the socket layer — deliberately, so a user's other devices stay in step (message-handler.service.ts:93-97 says so in a comment). The actor is known server-side the whole way (tasks.service.ts sets actorId; domain-event.listener.ts:131 publishes it as the message's top-level `userId`) but message-handler builds the client model as {type, data, push:{title,description,avatar,url}} and DROPS userId. So a listener CANNOT tell its own writes from anyone else's by inspecting the event. Do not go looking for an actorId in the payload again — it is not there, and that is intentional.

THE DESIGN: the writer records what it wrote (services/echo_log.py, keyed on remote task id, 30s expiry), and the subscriber skips an event whose task ids are ALL ours. TaskBridge notes every outbound write — _flush_row covers create/state/comment/time/attachment, and push() separately because it bypasses the outbox.

TWO THINGS THAT MUST NOT BE "SIMPLIFIED":
1. A time window ("ignore everything for N seconds after a flush") is one line and wrong: it drops a genuine concurrent change landing in that window, which defeats having a socket rather than a poll.
2. Suppression is decided per EVENT, before the debounce. After coalescing, a burst of our echoes would swallow a real change sharing the window.

EXTRACTING THE TASK ID: `taskId` wins over `id`. A comment event is {...commentViewModel, taskId, packageId}, so its `id` is the COMMENT; time entries and attachments nest their own ids too. Hence the shallow, precedence-ordered _task_ids, NOT the recursive walk _package_ids uses. Finding no id means reconcile — an unattributable event must never be suppressed.

Residual gap, accepted: someone else editing THE SAME task inside the window reads as our echo. Costs nothing while reconcile is create-only; revisit if the conflict policy lands and reconcile starts updating.

Measured live: a 29-task push went from 37 events / 7 board reads to 28 events / 28 suppressed / 0 reads, and a task created directly on the board still reconciled.
summary: asoode broadcasts every change to every member of a work package and applies NO actor exclusion at the socket layer...
title: The socket cannot recognise our own writes from the payload; the writer must record them

content: frontend/src/components/TaskListView.tsx follows asoode's WpListView.tsx and TaskDialog.tsx follows its TaskModal/TaskModalMain/TaskModalSidebar. Both apps use the same shadcn design tokens, so the classes ported almost verbatim. asoode groups a list by board column; this store has no columns, so the STATE is the group - which is why the group pill is painted with the state colour and the inline add row inside a group creates a task already in that state. State and priority colours in lib/tasks.ts are asoode's exact hex values so the two apps read the same way side by side. Within a state, `position` outranks priority in the sort - otherwise dragging a task past a higher-priority one would silently snap back. The task dialog sits at z-40, BELOW the app's Dialog layer (z-50) and toasts (z-100), so a confirm opened from inside it lands on top.
summary: The Tasks UI is a port of asoode's list mode and task modal: frontend/src/components/TaskListView
title: The Tasks UI is a port of asoode's list mode and task modal

content: Schema v5 adds tasks / task_comments / task_time_entries to the per-project DuckDB, plus sessions.last_seen_at. They are deliberately NOT a MemoryCategory: SYNC_CATEGORIES is derived automatically from the category enum (constants.py:24), so a task category would immediately start writing every task into the committed .claude-memory/*.json snapshot. Keeping them in their own tables is the whole reason the "JSON grows to 100MB" problem cannot happen. TestTasksStayOutOfTheSnapshot asserts it. The state vocabulary is asoode's WorkPackageTaskState verbatim (todo/in_progress/done/paused/blocked/cancelled/duplicate/incomplete/blocker) so the Phase 2 bridge maps names to ordinals losslessly. task_time_entries uses begin_at/end_at rather than begin/end because `end` is a DuckDB reserved word that cannot be used as a column name even in a plain SELECT.
summary: Schema v5 adds tasks / task_comments / task_time_entries to the per-project DuckDB, plus sessions
title: Tasks are separate DuckDB tables, never a MemoryCategory

content:
asoode's hierarchy is project -> work package (board) -> list (column) -> task. There is NO path that attaches a task to a project directly: POST /tasks/:listId/create is the only create route, and a listId only exists inside a work package. So a memory project can never be 'linked to an asoode project' - it links to one or more WORK PACKAGES, and linking to a project with no work package is not a state the API can represent. AsoodeBridge.bootstrap creates a work package precisely because of this, and attach() resolves a work package, never a project.

This generalises: every task platform worth supporting has a container level between the workspace and the task - Asana project/section, Monday board/group, Trello board/list, Jira project/board with an issue type. So the provider interface must model container-then-task as mandatory rather than treating the board as an asoode quirk. A provider that genuinely allowed a task with no container would supply a single implicit one rather than the interface making it optional.
summary: asoode's hierarchy is project -> work package (board) -> list (column) -> task
title: A task provider always has a board level; asoode has no tasks directly under a project

content:
VERIFIED 2026-09-04 by probing a real subagent, not inferred. docs/bridge/06-agent-team.md asserted throughout that "subagents inherit the session's MCP servers, so each agent can call memory_* directly" and nothing had ever checked it.

WHAT IS TRUE:
- All 66 mcp__memory__* tools are available to a subagent IMMEDIATELY. No ToolSearch, no extra configuration.
- memory_get_rules, memory_task_list and memory_search all succeeded from inside the subagent.
- The memory server's own SERVER INSTRUCTIONS are injected into the subagent verbatim too - inheritance covers instructions, not only tool schemas.
- The full WRITE surface comes with it: memory_store, memory_task_add, memory_task_done, memory_asoode_push. There is NO additional gate. Any dispatched agent can mutate the shared store and push to the live asoode board. An agent's tools list restricts its filesystem access; it does not restrain what it can do to the board.

TWO THINGS STILL UNKNOWN, because the probe used the built-in general-purpose agent which has tools: *:
- Whether an explicit `tools:` allowlist in a definition FILTERS inherited MCP tools. Until that is known, a definition should name its mcp__memory__* tools explicitly - it fails safe either way.
- Whether isolation: worktree behaves as the doc assumes (it claims isolation is per-agent, not per-task).

A SEPARATE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: memory_search does NOT search tasks. The probe searched "agent team" and got zero results while a task by that exact name sat in the queue. Memories and tasks are separate stores. Any agent told to "load context with memory_get_rules and memory_search" will silently miss everything in the task queue - it must also read memory_task_list / memory_task_get. All five agent definitions were amended for this.

OPERATIONAL FACT, learned the hard way: Claude Code enumerates ~/.claude/agents/ at SESSION START. Agents installed mid-session are NOT dispatchable until a restart - Agent(subagent_type="pm") returns "Agent type 'pm' not found". memory-mcp-setup's existing "Restart Claude Code" line now covers agents as well as MCP and hooks.

COST BASELINE: one subagent doing three read-only lookups cost 61,742 tokens and ~50 seconds. That is the floor for delegating anything at all, and it is the concrete argument behind the doc's rule to default to ONE agent and fan out only when the work is genuinely parallel.
summary: VERIFIED 2026-09-04 by probing a real subagent, not inferred
title: Subagents inherit the memory MCP server in full, including its write surface
